label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 5
knowledgePattern: Use perimeter scale to recover a right triangle from its altitude split
solution:
The altitude to the hypotenuse divides the right triangle into two smaller triangles, each similar to the original and therefore similar to one another. Their perimeter ratio equals their corresponding hypotenuse ratio, so AC:BC = 18:24 = 3:4.

Write AC=3u, BC=4u. Then AB=5u. By similarity, AD=AC2/AB=9u/5 and CD=AC·BC/AB=12u/5.

The perimeter of ACD is 3u+9u/5+12u/5=36u/5=18, giving u=5/2. Hence the required area is 12(3u)(4u)=6u2=75/2. Answer E.

hints.title: Match the similar right triangles
hints.body: Mark equal angles in the two small triangles and the original triangle. Match the side opposite the right angle in each.
hints.recap: Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles and the same ratio for all corresponding lengths.
hints.pitfall: Match hypotenuse to hypotenuse; the common altitude plays different side roles in the two triangles.
hints.pause: Use the two perimeters to find the ratio of the original legs.

recall.reminder: Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles and the same ratio for all corresponding lengths.

hints.title: Keep one unknown length scale
hints.body: Give the original legs a common scale consistent with their ratio. Use the right angle to recover the hypotenuse.
hints.recap: Pythagoras relates the two perpendicular legs to the hypotenuse.
hints.pitfall: A ratio fixes shape, but an actual perimeter is still needed to fix size.
hints.pause: Express the sides of one small triangle using that scale.

recall.reminder: Pythagoras relates the two perpendicular legs to the hypotenuse.

hints.title: Use one perimeter to fix size
hints.body: Translate the given perimeter of one small triangle into an equation for your common scale, then calculate the original triangle area.
hints.recap: Corresponding length ratios also compare perimeters; areas use the square of a length scale.
hints.pitfall: Do not use a length scale unchanged as an area scale.
hints.pause: Solve the scale equation and use the perpendicular original legs for the area.

recall.reminder: Corresponding length ratios also compare perimeters; areas use the square of a length scale.
